findings.title: Taking-back removals are skipped when the same hunk also has a kept addition
findings.why: The removal check is in an `elif` after `if kept:`. A single `-U0` hunk can both remove PR-added lines (a revert) and add other PR-owned lines. In that case `kept` is non-empty, so the `elif` never runs and the `(hunk.at, hunk.at)` place for the removed line is omitted. Example: the previous PR changes two adjacent base lines to A and B; a later round restores the base line where A was and changes B to C. `now` contains C, so `kept` is `[C]`, and the restored A line is never added to `Increment.lines`. The reviewer misses the revert. Check `hunk.removed` independently of `kept`.

findings.title: Path parsing from `diff --git` can misattribute hunks
findings.why: `_FILE` assumes an unquoted `a/... b/...` header and greedily splits at the last ` b/`. `core.quotePath=false` only stops octal quoting of non-ASCII; Git still C-quotes paths containing quotes, backslashes, tabs/newlines, and the two-path header is ambiguous for ordinary paths containing ` b/`. When the regex misses, `old_path`/`new_path` remain from the previous file (lines 48-49), so later hunks are recorded under the wrong path; when it matches the wrong ` b/`, the split is also wrong. A user's `diff.noprefix`/`diff.mnemonicPrefix` config likewise breaks the `a/`/`b/` assumption. The consequence is silently wrong or missing review lines.

findings.title: `splitlines()` lets file content inject fake diff headers
findings.why: `str.splitlines()` also splits on `\v`, `\f`, `\r`, U+2028, etc., not just `\n`. The diff is untrusted PR content; a changed line containing such a character followed by text like `diff --git a/x b/x` or `@@ -1 +1 @@` becomes a new physical line that matches `_FILE`/`_HUNK`. That resets the current path or adds a fake hunk, so an author can hide or misattribute changes in a later round. Splitting only on `\n` avoids this.

findings.title: Deleted/emptied files get a line 1 that is not in the head tree
findings.why: For a pure deletion hunk `new_count` is 0, so `new_start` is 0 (whole-file deletion) or the line before the removal; `max(new_start, 1)` turns a whole-file deletion/emptying into `at=1`. If that hunk removes lines the PR previously added, the taking-back branch at line 133 emits `{path: [(1,1)]}` even though `path` does not exist (or is empty) at `head`. `Increment.lines` is documented as head-side lines, so downstream comment/range lookup will fail or point at an unrelated line. Deleting a file the PR added is a common way to take it back, so this is reachable.

findings.title: Textconv is not disabled, so hunk line numbers can refer to converted text
findings.why: `--no-ext-diff` only disables external diff helpers. Git still runs configured `diff.<driver>.textconv` filters and emits hunks for the converted representation. The line numbers then do not correspond to the file at `head`, so `Increment.lines` can point at lines that do not exist (or are the wrong code) when a path has a textconv driver. Add `--no-textconv` or otherwise reject textconv.
